pr_title: Set Fronius entities to "unknown" when receiving invalid zero value
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Set entities to "unknown" when receiving invalid zero value.

Some devices may return `0` for their energy values while doing a firmware update. Setting them to "unknown" should avoid messing up statistics if that happens.

I've kept the state_class for "energy day" and "energy year" on TOTAL_INCREASING. These reset every day / year. 
Can someone confirm that this is correct?

Temporarily being 0 is a different problem from resetting/restarting from 0

Ie, doing this dance: 1000000, 0, 1000001 should be handled differently. Deltas will be broken. Better if the sensor goes unavailable when temporarily going to 0.

With TOTAL state class the difference should be fine after that dance, wouldn't it?

For the daily resetting (total increasing) sensor such a firmware-update bug would still mess up statistics. I guess finding out if the value is 0 because it resetted or because of API issues would always be a little hacky 😬.

Its unlikely to be exactly zero for long though. Perhaps unavailable when zero? 

Going to zero will still cause spikes in any delta calculations.

Joakim is right, this will still cause spikes, thus the thing this PR is trying to solved, won't be solved by this PR.

Marking it draft for now for that reason.

../Frenck

These entities will get `_attr_native_value=None` when zero now.
Should we keep `TOTAL` or revert to `TOTAL_INCREASING`?

Test is a bit tricky, as it needs to patch the fixture before loading. And I copied the wrong `freezer.tick` interval initially, so it kept failing 🐲
Should work now and can be used to test other things in the integration that aren't covered yet in future PRs.

review_comments: This will make it unknown rather than unavailable. Which probably is fine here. Maybe call the flag invalid_when_zero?
Oh, right thanks 👍. I did confuse these states 😬
Another way would be to just return without changing `_attr_native_value` and calling `async_write_ha_state` - which would just preserve the previous state. Would you prefer that over "unknown"?
Would mean different behavior on startup of ha compared to when running (unless we restore state), so i think going to unknown ls good enough.
You should return it unchanged if no patching is done. Running ky through loads/dumps is both slow and risk changing the fixture data in unplanned ways.

It is, isn't it? 
Line 49 is only invoked when patching. When not patching, the `load_fixture` function result is used directly (Line 48). 

And the whole function is not used when not patching any file - then `load_fixture` is used directly. Thus the same function signature of the patch and `load_fixture`.

Oh its that weird split i didnt understand.

A dict of fixes with the filename as key would make sense. Also i suggest you add the full filename. So the check is just:

```
if not (patch_values := patches.get(filename)):
  return text
```

The prefix to filename seem know at call site.
A dict seems like a good idea!
